name: LinkShortener.io
summary: Branded short links and dynamic QR codes with click reports by country and device, link-in-bio pages and your own domain on paid plans.
best_for: marketers and small teams who want branded short links and dynamic QR codes with click reports, and who are fine staying within a monthly link allowance
skip_if: you need an API to create links from your own software, you create thousands of links a month on a small budget, or you want a product we have tested ourselves
honest_knock: The Free plan allows only 20 links or QR codes a month and no custom domain. Changing where a live link points needs Pro at $34 a month. The pricing page says there is no public API on any plan. In our test on 18 November 2026 the app also offered two $6 plans, for QR codes only or link in bio only, that the pricing page does not list.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Basic · Basic $13 a month or $130 a year (350 links or QR codes a month, 1 custom domain)
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-18 on linkshortener.io/pricing, US dollars, and in our own test that day; earlier: read 2026-11-12) LinkShortener.io has a Free plan and three paid plans, each with a shared monthly allowance of short links and QR codes. Free costs $0 for 20 a month on the shared tli.sh domain and needs an account but no card. Basic costs $13 a month, or $130 a year, for 350 a month and 1 custom domain. Pro costs $34 a month, or $340 a year, for 2,000 a month and 3 custom domains. Elite costs $260 a month, or $2,600 a year, for 5,000 a month, 10 custom domains and a dedicated account manager. Enterprise has no listed price and covers unlimited volume, SSO and white-label options. The page says clicks and scans are never billed and no plan has overage fees: when you reach your monthly allowance, existing links keep working and new links wait until the allowance renews or you upgrade. Yearly billing is shown as two months free. The page puts custom URL slugs and changing where a live link points on Pro and above, and says Basic and the free plan do not include destination editing. In our test on 18 November 2026 the free account had no custom slug and no Edit option, and the app showed that Basic can change a QR code's destination but not a short link's. The app's upgrade screen also offered two $6 plans, one for QR codes only and one for link in bio only, which the pricing page does not list. We did not pay, so the tax added is not known.

schema_offer.description: Basic, Basic $13 a month or $130 a year (350 links or QR codes a month, 1 custom domain); Pro $34 a month or $340 a year (2,000, 3 domains); Elite $260 a month or $2,600 a year (5,000, 10 domains); Free is $0 with 20 links or QR codes a month; Enterprise is custom. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-18.

recent_change.text: LinkShortener.io now includes a Broken Link Checker on the Pro and Elite plans. It checks the target page about a minute after a link is created or edited, on every click or scan, and nightly, and emails the account owner when a page stops working.

claims.observed: The account page shows 20 links or QR codes a month on Free, as the dossier says; the counter read 20/20 after two links were made, so whether it counts down was not checked, and the behaviour at the limit was not tested.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Plans page was read without clicking an upgrade button
claims.comparability: The dossier allowance against the counter text and the Free plan card; the limit itself was not reached.
claims.buying_consequence: The Free allowance is small: 20 links or QR codes a month, shared.

claims.claim: You have reached your custom domain limit.
claims.observed: The Free plan has no custom domain: the account says the custom domain limit is reached, the menu item Custom Domains carries an Upgrade label and the form marks custom domain as a paid feature.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Plans page was read without clicking an upgrade button
claims.comparability: The dossier knock about a custom domain against the account text and the menu; a custom domain was not set up.
claims.buying_consequence: Branded short links on your own domain need a paid plan, so Free links use the shared short domain of the service.

claims.observed: curl -I on both short links gave HTTP/2 302 with the right Location (with the UTM parameter on the first), no-store caching, in 0.12 to 0.23 seconds, with no interstitial page and no advertisement.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Plans page was read without clicking an upgrade button
claims.comparability: A measured redirect against no stored claim about speed or interstitials; three requests from one location on one day.
claims.buying_consequence: The redirect is fast and clean on Free, with no page in between.

claims.observed: The first browser visit showed as 1 click about 10 seconds later and the second made it 2; three curl requests were not counted, so bots seem filtered. Country and device reports were not checked.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Plans page was read without clicking an upgrade button
claims.comparability: Two browser visits and three curl requests on two links; no stored claim about click counting exists and the dossier says only click reports.
claims.buying_consequence: Click counts follow real browser visits quickly, but the reports by country and device were not seen.

claims.observed: The UTM fields (Source, Medium, Campaign, Term, Content) work on Free and the redirect adds the parameter, although the UTM table on the link page stayed empty.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Plans page was read without clicking an upgrade button
claims.comparability: The Free plan line UTM Builder against a redirect checked with curl on one link; the empty table was not explained.
claims.buying_consequence: Campaign tagging is included in the free plan.

claims.observed: On Free the Random path switch cannot be turned off, so no own slug can be chosen; URL Customisation is a Pro feature.
claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Plans page was read without clicking an upgrade button
claims.comparability: A form setting seen on one Free account; no stored claim about own slugs exists.
claims.buying_consequence: Short links on Free cannot carry a readable name.

claims.observed: Custom domain, country and device redirects, expiry, password, social preview, time-based redirects and open in app are paid; the Edit button on an existing link carries the label Upgrade. claims.plan: No plan was bought; the Plans page was read without clicking an upgrade button
claims.comparability: Labels in the app and on the Plans page against no stored claim; no paid plan was used.
claims.buying_consequence: A wrong destination on a short link cannot be corrected on Free or Basic.

claims.observed: Besides Free, Basic, Pro and Elite the Plans page lists QR code only at $6 (20 QR codes a month), Link in bio only at $6 and Enterprise on request (10,000); the dossier mentions a Free plan and three paid plans.

claims.comparability: The dossier plan count against the Plans page of 18 November; the $6 plans were not opened.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested LinkShortener.io in our existing free account: two short links to our own sites were made in about a minute and 4 steps; curl showed a direct 302 with the right target in 0.12 to 0.23 seconds, with no interstitial page and no advertisement; a browser click showed in the statistics after about 10 seconds while curl requests were not counted; UTM fields and a QR code per link work on Free. On Free there is no own slug, editing an existing link is behind Upgrade and custom domain, password and social preview are paid; changing the destination of a short link needs Pro. The prices match the dossier, and the app also lists two plans of $6. Deleting the test links gave a server error, so they are still active. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used our existing LinkShortener.io account on the Free plan, with the interface in English (no language setting was found). The test started at 09:48:53. The onboarding (Set up your links the correct way) asked 3 questions, each with a Pro option and a free option (a branded domain, an email when a link breaks, a branded QR code); the free options were chosen (the short domain of the service, You check your links yourself, Plain QR codes, with our name under them), and the page ended with the line Pro adds all three, for $34 a month. Start Pro, which was not clicked. The business name field was filled with our name and was changed to Test Co. Core action: two short links were made, to two of our own sites. The first link was made in about 1 minute and 4 steps (name, destination, UTM fields, Create) and got a short link on the shared short domain of the service. The UTM fields (Source, Medium, Campaign, Term, Content) work on Free, with the text To make use of Google Analytics, the Source, Medium, and Campaign parameters are required.; the UTM table on the link page stayed empty, but the redirect did add the parameter. Click statistics: 3 curl requests were NOT counted (filtered as bots); the first browser visit at 09:50:02 showed as 1 click (This Week 1, All Clicks 1) about 10 seconds later, a second visit made it 2, and the second link also showed 1. The country map said No country data available at first and then showed a map; per country and device reports were not checked because the visits came from one browser. Limits on Free: the Random path switch cannot be turned off on Free, so there is no own slug (URL Customisation is Pro); custom domain, country and device redirects are marked Paid feature, and the form shows expiry, password, social preview, time-based redirects and open in app as paid options; the Edit button on an existing link carries the label Upgrade. Every link has a black and white QR code with Download PNG and Download SVG, no logo; the separate QR list was empty (No records found) and no separate QR was made, because it uses the same allowance. The account page says Links and QR Codes remaining: 20/20 (Refreshing in 4 weeks from now) and You have reached your custom domain limit. Plans, read up to the payment step on the Plans page (US dollars, nothing filled in): Free $0 (20 links or QR codes per month, UTM Builder, Basic Analytics); Basic $13 a month ($10.83 a month yearly, Billed annually: $130 a year; 350 links or QR codes, 1 custom domain, edit the destination of a QR code); Pro $34 ($340 a year; 2,000, 3 custom domains, URL Customisation, edit the destination of a short link, broken link checker); Elite $260 ($2,600 a year; 5,000, 10 custom domains); QR code only $6 (20 QR codes per month); Link in bio only $6; Enterprise on request (10,000). The banner says 12 months for the price of 10. Deviations from the dossier: the prices and allowances of Free, Basic, Pro and Elite match. The dossier text says a Free plan and three paid plans; the app also lists two plans of $6 (QR code only and Link in bio only) and Enterprise on request. Basic may change only the destination of a QR code, and changing the destination of a short link needs Pro. The price fields of our pages are not touched. Checkout: NOT reached. No Upgrade or Start Pro button was clicked, so no tax, total or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: Free, no subscription, so nothing to cancel. Not tested: an own domain (not allowed), the paid plans, what happens at 20 of 20, reports per country and device (the map was empty for visits from one browser), the broken link checker, Link in bio, Bulk CSV import and the migration tool. Clean up: the bulk action Delete selected Links gave 500 SERVER ERROR and a second try did nothing visible; the Active switch on the link page could not be operated. So both test links are still active (they redirect to our own sites and were shared nowhere). The business name is now Test Co. All tabs were closed.
exit_test.awkward: On Free the Random path switch cannot be turned off, so you cannot choose your own slug, and the Edit button on an existing link is behind Upgrade. Changing where a short link points needs Pro; Basic can change only the QR destination, so a mistake in the destination cannot be fixed on the cheaper plans. Deleting links gave a 500 server error, and the links stayed active. The app lists two plans of $6 that the dossier does not mention.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested LinkShortener.io in our existing free account: two short links to our own sites were made in about a minute and 4 steps; curl showed a direct 302 with the right target in 0.12 to 0.23 seconds, with no interstitial page and no advertisement; a browser click showed in the statistics after about 10 seconds while curl requests were not counted; UTM fields and a QR code per link work on Free. On Free there is no own slug, editing an existing link is behind Upgrade and custom domain, password and social preview are paid; changing the destination of a short link needs Pro. The prices match the dossier, and the app also lists two plans of $6. Deleting the test links gave a server error, so they are still active. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used our existing LinkShortener.io account on the Free plan, with the interface in English (no language setting was found). The test started at 09:48:53. The onboarding (Set up your links the correct way) asked 3 questions, each with a Pro option and a free option (a branded domain, an email when a link breaks, a branded QR code); the free options were chosen (the short domain of the service, You check your links yourself, Plain QR codes, with our name under them), and the page ended with the line Pro adds all three, for $34 a month. Start Pro, which was not clicked. The business name field was filled with our name and was changed to Test Co. Core action: two short links were made, to two of our own sites. The first link was made in about 1 minute and 4 steps (name, destination, UTM fields, Create) and got a short link on the shared short domain of the service. The UTM fields (Source, Medium, Campaign, Term, Content) work on Free, with the text To make use of Google Analytics, the Source, Medium, and Campaign parameters are required.; the UTM table on the link page stayed empty, but the redirect did add the parameter. Click statistics: 3 curl requests were NOT counted (filtered as bots); the first browser visit at 09:50:02 showed as 1 click (This Week 1, All Clicks 1) about 10 seconds later, a second visit made it 2, and the second link also showed 1. The country map said No country data available at first and then showed a map; per country and device reports were not checked because the visits came from one browser. Limits on Free: the Random path switch cannot be turned off on Free, so there is no own slug (URL Customisation is Pro); custom domain, country and device redirects are marked Paid feature, and the form shows expiry, password, social preview, time-based redirects and open in app as paid options; the Edit button on an existing link carries the label Upgrade. Every link has a black and white QR code with Download PNG and Download SVG, no logo; the separate QR list was empty (No records found) and no separate QR was made, because it uses the same allowance. The account page says Links and QR Codes remaining: 20/20 (Refreshing in 4 weeks from now) and You have reached your custom domain limit. Plans, read up to the payment step on the Plans page (US dollars, nothing filled in): Free $0 (20 links or QR codes per month, UTM Builder, Basic Analytics); Basic $13 a month ($10.83 a month yearly, Billed annually: $130 a year; 350 links or QR codes, 1 custom domain, edit the destination of a QR code); Pro $34 ($340 a year; 2,000, 3 custom domains, URL Customisation, edit the destination of a short link, broken link checker); Elite $260 ($2,600 a year; 5,000, 10 custom domains); QR code only $6 (20 QR codes per month); Link in bio only $6; Enterprise on request (10,000). The banner says 12 months for the price of 10. Deviations from the dossier: the prices and allowances of Free, Basic, Pro and Elite match. The dossier text says a Free plan and three paid plans; the app also lists two plans of $6 (QR code only and Link in bio only) and Enterprise on request. Basic may change only the destination of a QR code, and changing the destination of a short link needs Pro. The price fields of our pages are not touched. Checkout: NOT reached. No Upgrade or Start Pro button was clicked, so no tax, total or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: Free, no subscription, so nothing to cancel. Not tested: an own domain (not allowed), the paid plans, what happens at 20 of 20, reports per country and device (the map was empty for visits from one browser), the broken link checker, Link in bio, Bulk CSV import and the migration tool. Clean up: the bulk action Delete selected Links gave 500 SERVER ERROR and a second try did nothing visible; the Active switch on the link page could not be operated. So both test links are still active (they redirect to our own sites and were shared nowhere). The business name is now Test Co. All tabs were closed.
exit_test.awkward: On Free the Random path switch cannot be turned off, so you cannot choose your own slug, and the Edit button on an existing link is behind Upgrade. Changing where a short link points needs Pro; Basic can change only the QR destination, so a mistake in the destination cannot be fixed on the cheaper plans. Deleting links gave a 500 server error, and the links stayed active. The app lists two plans of $6 that the dossier does not mention.
